claims.text: Brent crude futures fell $1.54, or 1.47%, to $103.18 a barrel following announcements regarding Russian diesel supplies and a proposed energy ceasefire.

US President Donald Trump stated that Russia would immediately supply over 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes shortly after.
US President Donald Trump announced on October 11, 2026, that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities.
A bipartisan group of seven US senators issued a statement calling on President Donald Trump to reverse course on his diesel deal with Russia.
US Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Russia's war against Ukraine.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the Russia diesel agreement, stating the Trump administration would follow through using existing legal authority to lower prices.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that the diesel deal with Russia "is in direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada, and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe."
US President Donald Trump previously announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on September 14, 2026, but Russian President Vladimir Putin rebuffed the proposal.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that Russian forces attacked a power plant in Kharkiv and launched glide bombs and drones across Ukraine despite Trump's energy ceasefire announcement.

On October 10, 2026, US President Donald Trump warned Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian oil refineries and urged Ukrainians to replace their leader through new elections.
The US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7, 2026, as part of the deal announced by President Donald Trump.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told state news agency Tass that Russian diesel exports could reach 3 million tonnes per month in the future.
According to the AAA, the average diesel price in the United States was $6.28 per gallon, down from a record high of $6.53 recorded in late September.
The Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers reported that air strikes on a gold mine near the Sudan-Egypt border killed at least 72 civilian workers on October 10, 2026.
Emergency Lawyers accused the Egyptian air force of conducting the air strike on the Jabal al-Uqaydat gold mining site.
An air strike on the same mining site at Jabal al-Uqaydat in June 2026 killed 23 workers.
Both Sudan and Egypt claim ownership of the resource-rich Halayeb triangle border territory.
The Egyptian military reported detaining 223 people, including 136 foreign nationals, during a border security operation against illegal gold mining in June 2026.
Eyewitnesses stated that aircraft fired more than five missiles directly at miners' camps and excavation pits at the border gold mine.
The ongoing civil war in Sudan has led to a surge in artisanal gold mining conducted by civilians using rudimentary tools in remote border regions.
The Sudan Doctors Network warned that the death toll from the gold mine air strike was expected to increase due to severe injuries and limited access to medical care.
According to the UK think tank Chatham House, up to 60% of Sudan's unofficial gold exports end up in Egypt.
Rights groups reported that the air strike on the gold mine near the Egypt-Sudan border injured more than 50 people.
A boat carrying 305 migrants, predominantly from Ethiopia, capsized off the eastern coast of Djibouti near Guhere during the night of October 8-9, 2026.
The International Organization for Migration reported that at least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died and 84 remained missing after the boat capsized off Djibouti.
At least 82 people survived the boat capsizing off Djibouti, all of whom were Ethiopian nationals.
Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, said survivors told him "that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it."

IOM Director General Amy Pope urged action from governments and donors, stating, "No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way. We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives."
The International Organization for Migration recorded more than 20,000 migrant movements from Ethiopia to Djibouti between September 10 and October 2026.
More than 900 migrants died or went missing while attempting the sea route between the Horn of Africa and Yemen in 2025.
A similar migrant boat shipwreck off the coast of Djibouti in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.
